Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 20(d) imposes a blanket assignment prohibition on both parties with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent — the playbook walk-away position. Section 3(c) compounds this by separately barring Sparkling from assigning absent Garman's written consent, and Section 2 grants only a "non-transferable" licence. There is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right elsewhere (Section 17 has no such trigger), so the fix is to add the affiliate/successor carve-out for us, a reasonableness standard for other assignments, a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors, and express confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) is conformed by cross-reference.

Original paragraphs:
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0142: (d) Except as expressly permitted below, neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Sparkling may assign this Agreement, without the consent of Garman, to an affiliate of Sparkling or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or shares, and no such transaction or change of control of Sparkling shall constitute a breach of this Agreement or entitle Garman to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement. Garman may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Sparkling.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as permitted by Section 20(d) or as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;

Comment:
[Playbook] We added the customary carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, confirmed no Garman right arises on our change of control, and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard with no assignment by Garman to our competitors. As a fallback we can accept mutual assignment to successors on written notice with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check appears to be a phrasing-variant miss — the operative sentence does read 'Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time, in whole or in part, for convenience' — and the 0.434 changed-character ratio is explained by the two notice-period substitutions plus the appended refund sentence, so neither undermines the edit.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

paragraphs.text: 19. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES

During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
11. FEES
Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.

Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322
7. OPTION TO REJECT SOFTWARE

If during the acceptance period described in Section 6, the Software has failed to perform in accordance with the Specifications and Garman has been unable to correct the deficiency within 45 business days of written notice being provided to Garman of such failure then Sparkling shall have the option, exercisable on 15 business days written notice to Garman, in lieu of any other remedy, to reject the Software. Such option shall terminate if in the interim, the Software successfully completes acceptance testing and meets the Specifications.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
input.rationale: The grant is perpetual and not revocable at will (Section 17(a) keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, with termination only on insolvency or uncured 30-day default), so the term aspect is compliant. However, the licence covers only affiliated companies "operating at Authorized Locations" and says nothing about contractors or outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, and it is expressly "non-transferable", reinforced by Section 3(c) and Section 20(d) which bar assignment without Garman's consent — leaving no successor-transfer path in an M&A transaction. We therefore added affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, a successor-transfer right, and conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d).

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to Sparkling's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and permit transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the licence to our affiliated companies and to contractors and outsourced service providers using the Software on our behalf, and added a successor-transfer right, with conforming changes to Sections 3(c) and 20(d). Our playbook requires operational use by affiliates and contractors and continuity of the licence through a merger or sale of the business; the perpetual term in Section 17(a) is acceptable as drafted.

payload.rationale: The grant is perpetual and not revocable at will (Section 17(a) keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, with termination only on insolvency or uncured 30-day default), so the term aspect is compliant. However, the licence covers only affiliated companies "operating at Authorized Locations" and says nothing about contractors or outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, and it is expressly "non-transferable", reinforced by Section 3(c) and Section 20(d) which bar assignment without Garman's consent — leaving no successor-transfer path in an M&A transaction. We therefore added affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, a successor-transfer right, and conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d).

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

content.text: No audit, inspection, or usage-verification right against Sparkling exists anywhere in the agreement. The only examination right runs in our favour (escrow materials, p0114), and the only Sparkling reporting duty is a one-time post-termination destruction certificate (p0118), not a recurring audit.

input.quote: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
input.rationale: The use restrictions in § 3 (p0031–p0039), the licence grant in § 2, § 14 (confidentiality), § 17 and the general provisions in § 20 contain no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right exercisable by Garman against Sparkling, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "access", "premises" and "remote" return no such right. The only examination right (p0114, escrow materials) runs in our favour, and p0118 imposes only a one-time post-termination certification of destruction, not a recurring audit or any access to Sparkling systems. Since the rule constrains audit rights binding the Customer, their complete absence is at or better than the preferred position, and no redline is warranted (raising the issue would risk inviting an audit right).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:

input.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment penalty or minimum/early-termination fee payable by Sparkling. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "interest" and "shall pay" return only Section 11 (payment of fees per the Fee Schedule). Section 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination charge, Section 17(c) converts the licence to a perpetual, fee-free licence and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees on Garman's default, and Section 8 requires Garman to refund all amounts if Sparkling rejects the Software. Section 19 non-solicitation carries no stipulated payment. All money flows on early exit therefore run in our favour, meeting the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 2 licence grant scope**

**What I found**

- **Term is fine.** Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid, terminable only on insolvency events or an uncured 30-day material default (p0127), and Section 17 even converts it to a fee-free perpetual licence if we terminate for Garman's default. So the licence is *not* revocable at Garman's discretion — no issue there.
- **Affiliates only partially covered.** The grant runs to "affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations" — a narrower scope than our playbook requires.
- **Contractors excluded.** No coverage for contractors or outsourced service providers using the Software on our behalf, and Section 3(c) bars sublicence/transfer to "any Person" without Garman's written consent.
- **No successor transfer.** The licence is "non-transferable" and Section 20(d) (p0142) requires consent for any assignment, so a merger or sale of our business would strand the licence.

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**

1. **p0028** — grant extended to Sparkling, its affiliated companies and contractors/outsourced service providers acting on its behalf; "non-transferable" deleted and replaced with transferability to a successor to all or substantially all of our business or assets.
2. **p0033 (§3(c))** — conforming carve-outs for affiliates/contractors under Section 2 and for successor transfers.
3. **p0142 (§20(d))** — mutual carve-out permitting assignment without consent to a successor by merger, reorganization or sale.

This reaches the preferred position with three surgical edits; no changes were needed to the term/termination provisions, which already favour us.

Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The grant is perpetual and not revocable at will (Section 17(a) keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, with termination only on insolvency or uncured 30-day default), so the term aspect is compliant. However, the licence covers only affiliated companies "operating at Authorized Locations" and says nothing about contractors or outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, and it is expressly "non-transferable", reinforced by Section 3(c) and Section 20(d) which bar assignment without Garman's consent — leaving no successor-transfer path in an M&A transaction. We therefore added affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, a successor-transfer right, and conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d).

Original paragraphs:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0028: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors and outsourced service providers acting on Sparkling's behalf, a non-exclusive licence, transferable to a successor to all or substantially all of Sparkling's business or assets, to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation. Sparkling's right, if any, to use the Software and Documentation at locations other than the Authorized Locations is subject to the payment of additional fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule.
p0033: (c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except (i) to affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors and outsourced service providers acting on Sparkling's behalf as contemplated by Section 2, (ii) to a successor to all or substantially all of Sparkling's business or assets, or (iii) as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
p0142: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, except that either party may assign this Agreement, without such consent, to a successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets by merger, reorganization or sale.

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the licence to our affiliated companies and to contractors and outsourced service providers using the Software on our behalf, and added a successor-transfer right, with conforming changes to Sections 3(c) and 20(d). Our playbook requires operational use by affiliates and contractors and continuity of the licence through a merger or sale of the business; the perpetual term in Section 17(a) is acceptable as drafted.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right over Sparkling. I confirmed this by reading the likely homes for such a right — § 2 (grant), § 3 plus its continuation (use restrictions, (a)–(g)), § 14 (confidentiality), § 20 and its continuation (general matters) — and by searching for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, compliance, records, access, premises, remote, certif*.

The only two near-hits both fall outside the rule:
- **p0114 (escrow)** — an examination/testing right held by *Sparkling*, i.e. in our favour.
- **p0118 (termination)** — a single post-termination certificate that Sparkling has ceased use; not a recurring audit and no access to our systems.

Because AUDIT constrains audit rights *binding the Customer*, their total absence sits at or above our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access). I deliberately recommend no edit here: proposing audit machinery would invite a right that does not currently exist. Worth monitoring only if Garman later seeks a verification clause in negotiation, at which point the preferred parameters should be inserted in § 3.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The use restrictions in § 3 (p0031–p0039), the licence grant in § 2, § 14 (confidentiality), § 17 and the general provisions in § 20 contain no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right exercisable by Garman against Sparkling, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "access", "premises" and "remote" return no such right. The only examination right (p0114, escrow materials) runs in our favour, and p0118 imposes only a one-time post-termination certification of destruction, not a recurring audit or any access to Sparkling systems. Since the rule constrains audit rights binding the Customer, their complete absence is at or better than the preferred position, and no redline is warranted (raising the issue would risk inviting an audit right).

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee on us:

- **Section 11 (p0084)** is a bare obligation to pay fees per the Fee Schedule — no penalty or default interest mechanic anywhere in the document (searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty" and "interest" return nothing relevant).
- **Section 17(b) (p0118)** gives us termination for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no** exit fee or remaining-contract-value liability.
- **Section 17(c) (p0128)** and **Section 8 (p0057)** both run in our favour: on Garman's default the licence converts to a perpetual fee-free licence with a refund of fees for services not rendered, and on rejection of the Software Garman refunds all amounts paid.
- **Section 19** non-solicitation is mutual and carries no stipulated damages figure.

No fallback (3-month cap on an early-termination fee) is needed, since no such fee exists to cap.

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment penalty or minimum/early-termination fee payable by Sparkling. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "interest" and "shall pay" return only Section 11 (payment of fees per the Fee Schedule). Section 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination charge, Section 17(c) converts the licence to a perpetual, fee-free licence and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees on Garman's default, and Section 8 requires Garman to refund all amounts if Sparkling rejects the Software. Section 19 non-solicitation carries no stipulated payment. All money flows on early exit therefore run in our favour, meeting the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

The only examination right (p0114, escrow materials) runs in our favour, and p0118 imposes only a one-time post-termination certification of destruction, not a recurring audit or any access to Sparkling systems. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right over Sparkling. I confirmed this by reading the likely homes for such a right — § 2 (grant), § 3 plus its continuation (use restrictions, (a)–(g)), § 14 (confidentiality), § 20 and its continuation (general matters) — and by searching for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, compliance, records, access, premises, remote, certif*.

The only two near-hits both fall outside the rule:
- **p0114 (escrow)** — an examination/testing right held by *Sparkling*, i.e. in our favour.
- **p0118 (termination)** — a single post-termination certificate that Sparkling has ceased use; not a recurring audit and no access to our systems.

Because AUDIT constrains audit rights *binding the Customer*, their total absence sits at or above our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access). I deliberately recommend no edit here: proposing audit machinery would invite a right that does not currently exist. input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto" — i.e. the bespoke Modifications (Schedule "D") that Sparkling commissions and pays for — with no licence back beyond the narrow, non-transferable use licence in Section 2. The Agreement contains no ownership provision for Sparkling's data at all, even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting Sparkling's data. That breaches the playbook position that we own what we pay for and retain all rights in our data. Garman's ownership of its pre-existing platform is acceptable, so the redline preserves that while vesting the paid-for Modifications in Sparkling (with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman IP), confirming Sparkling's ownership of its data (including converted data), and excluding joint ownership.

proposal.summary: Limit Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Work, give Sparkling ownership of paid-for Modifications with a licence back to embedded Garman IP, and confirm Sparkling owns its data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Software and Documentation, so that the Modifications and other work product we commission and pay for vest in us (with a perpetual licence back to any Garman IP embedded in them), and we have confirmed that we retain all rights in our data, including data converted under Section 4. Our playbook position is that we own what we fund and everything we put in, with no assignment of our IP or data to the vendor and no joint ownership; if Garman must retain title to modifications of its own code, we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Modifications for our business instead of the assignment.

Except as expressly provided in this Agreement, no title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.

Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling's data, including data converted pursuant to Section 4, and Garman acquires no rights in such data. Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. input.summary: Limit Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Work, give Sparkling ownership of paid-for Modifications with a licence back to embedded Garman IP, and confirm Sparkling owns its data.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have limited Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Software and Documentation, so that the Modifications and other work product we commission and pay for vest in us (with a perpetual licence back to any Garman IP embedded in them), and we have confirmed that we retain all rights in our data, including data converted under Section 4. Our playbook position is that we own what we fund and everything we put in, with no assignment of our IP or data to the vendor and no joint ownership; if Garman must retain title to modifications of its own code, we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Modifications for our business instead of the assignment.

ops.text: Sparkling is and shall remain the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Modifications and any other work product developed specifically for Sparkling and paid for by Sparkling under this Agreement (collectively, the "Sparkling Deliverables"), and Garman hereby assigns to Sparkling all right, title and interest in the Sparkling Deliverables. input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto" — i.e. the bespoke Modifications (Schedule "D") that Sparkling commissions and pays for — with no licence back beyond the narrow, non-transferable use licence in Section 2. The Agreement contains no ownership provision for Sparkling's data at all, even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting Sparkling's data. That breaches the playbook position that we own what we pay for and retain all rights in our data. Garman's ownership of its pre-existing platform is acceptable, so the redline preserves that while vesting the paid-for Modifications in Sparkling (with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman IP), confirming Sparkling's ownership of its data (including converted data), and excluding joint ownership.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322
11. FEES
Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.

The redline reaches the playbook position: it adds affiliates plus contractors/outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, strikes 'non-transferable' and adds an express successor-transfer right, and makes conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d) so the grant is not undercut elsewhere.

The changed-character ratios are high only because the grant and assignment sentences must be restructured to insert the licensee-side parties and the successor carve-out; no unrelated concessions or new obligations were introduced, so the advisory minimality flags are acceptable here.

Directionally correct for the customer and internally consistent: the Authorized Location limitation survives in clause (i) and the additional-fee sentence, so removing the trailing 'operating at Authorized Locations' phrase from the affiliate reference does not covertly expand geographic scope.

Comment is accurate and appropriately scoped — it concedes that the perpetual term in Section 17(a) already satisfies the no-at-will-revocation element, cites the playbook basis, and explains the conforming edits in one or two sentences in the required voice. Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Garman may charge a fee at its rates set out in the Fee Schedule to provide Software Repair Services which are required due to:
(1) failure due to Sparkling operator errors;

(2) failure to maintain Software at such updated version or release of the Software provided by Garman to Sparkling, from time to time, at no additional charge as part of the Maintenance Services or otherwise;
(3) material modification of the Software by Sparkling; or
(4) the Software being transferred to a different networking environment or hardware configuration without the prior written consent of Garman; or
(5) any failure of the hardware or the operating system not caused by Garman or the Software.
17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right over Sparkling. I confirmed this by reading the likely homes for such a right — § 2 (grant), § 3 plus its continuation (use restrictions, (a)–(g)), § 14 (confidentiality), § 20 and its continuation (general matters) — and by searching for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, compliance, records, access, premises, remote, certif*.

The only two near-hits both fall outside the rule:
- **p0114 (escrow)** — an examination/testing right held by *Sparkling*, i.e. in our favour.
- **p0118 (termination)** — a single post-termination certificate that Sparkling has ceased use; not a recurring audit and no access to our systems.

Because AUDIT constrains audit rights *binding the Customer*, their total absence sits at or above our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access). I deliberately recommend no edit here: proposing audit machinery would invite a right that does not currently exist. Worth monitoring only if Garman later seeks a verification clause in negotiation, at which point the preferred parameters should be inserted in § 3.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 13, ¶p0088**

Section 13 vests in Garman "all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)" and states that no title passes to Sparkling. Because "Modifications" are the bespoke changes in Schedule "D" that Sparkling commissions and pays for, Garman would own work product we fund, with only the narrow non-transferable use licence in Section 2 coming back to us. Separately, the Agreement is silent on ownership of Sparkling's data, despite Section 4(b) requiring Garman to convert it.

Redline (validated, preferred level):
- Narrows Garman's ownership to the Work "as it exists independently of this Agreement" (its platform ownership is unobjectionable) and makes the no-title sentence subject to the Agreement's express grants.
- Adds a new paragraph: Sparkling owns the Modifications and other work product developed specifically for and paid for by it (Garman assigns), with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman background IP; Sparkling retains all rights in its data, including data converted under Section 4; no joint ownership.
- Fallback offered in the comment: Garman may keep title to modifications of its own code if we receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them.

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto" — i.e. the bespoke Modifications (Schedule "D") that Sparkling commissions and pays for — with no licence back beyond the narrow, non-transferable use licence in Section 2. The Agreement contains no ownership provision for Sparkling's data at all, even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting Sparkling's data. That breaches the playbook position that we own what we pay for and retain all rights in our data. Garman's ownership of its pre-existing platform is acceptable, so the redline preserves that while vesting the paid-for Modifications in Sparkling (with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman IP), confirming Sparkling's ownership of its data (including converted data), and excluding joint ownership.

p0088: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.

Except as expressly provided in this Agreement, no title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
Sparkling is and shall remain the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Modifications and any other work product developed specifically for Sparkling and paid for by Sparkling under this Agreement (collectively, the "Sparkling Deliverables"), and Garman hereby assigns to Sparkling all right, title and interest in the Sparkling Deliverables. To the extent any intellectual property of Garman existing independently of this Agreement is embedded in the Sparkling Deliverables, Garman grants Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense such intellectual property as part of the Sparkling Deliverables. Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling's data, including data converted pursuant to Section 4, and Garman acquires no rights in such data. [Playbook] We have limited Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Software and Documentation, so that the Modifications and other work product we commission and pay for vest in us (with a perpetual licence back to any Garman IP embedded in them), and we have confirmed that we retain all rights in our data, including data converted under Section 4. Our playbook position is that we own what we fund and everything we put in, with no assignment of our IP or data to the vendor and no joint ownership; if Garman must retain title to modifications of its own code, we can accept a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Modifications for our business instead of the assignment.

input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the General Matters provisions (Section 20(a)-(j), p0135-p0149) contain no insurance covenant. Insurance is required here because Garman is not a mere shrink-wrap licensor: under Section 4(a) its personnel deliver and install the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location (on-premises work), and under Section 4(b) Garman performs conversion of "Sparkling's data" for future installations, with Section 9(a) requiring us to provide information about our operations and internal procedures. That combination of premises access and data processing is exactly the profile the playbook requires to be insured, and the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor that processes data or works on our premises. The gap is aggravated because Section 15 limits Garman's liability, so uninsured exposure would sit with us. The obligation runs against the counterparty, so there is no direction problem. Minimal fix: insert a new Section 20(k) after the entire-agreement subsection tracking the model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), surviving one year post-term. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is flagged in the comment if Garman cannot obtain the preferred limits.

input.quote: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the General Matters provisions (Section 20(a)-(j), p0135-p0149) contain no insurance covenant. Insurance is required here because Garman is not a mere shrink-wrap licensor: under Section 4(a) its personnel deliver and install the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location (on-premises work), and under Section 4(b) Garman performs conversion of "Sparkling's data" for future installations, with Section 9(a) requiring us to provide information about our operations and internal procedures. That combination of premises access and data processing is exactly the profile the playbook requires to be insured, and the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor that processes data or works on our premises. The gap is aggravated because Section 15 limits Garman's liability, so uninsured exposure would sit with us. The obligation runs against the counterparty, so there is no direction problem. Minimal fix: insert a new Section 20(k) after the entire-agreement subsection tracking the model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), surviving one year post-term. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is flagged in the comment if Garman cannot obtain the preferred limits.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: The Software conformance warranty duration meets the preferred position (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and continuing while under maintenance), and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer that would swallow it. However, Section 12 states no remedy for breach: the only repair path is Garman's "best efforts" repair under the Maintenance Services (p0077), which is fee-bearing in listed cases and carries no replacement or refund backstop, and the refund/rejection right in Sections 7-8 expires with the acceptance period. Section 12 also omits a professional and workmanlike warranty for Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance), a no-malicious-code warranty and a compliance-with-laws warranty. We inserted those warranties and an express repair, replacement or re-performance remedy with a refund if Garman fails to cure within 30 days.

proposal.summary: Add services/malicious code/compliance warranties and an express repair-replace-or-refund remedy to Section 12
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 12 warrants Software conformance for a year but gives no stated remedy and says nothing about the services, malicious code or legal compliance, so we added a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus a repair, re-performance or refund remedy. If helpful we can accept a 90-day services warranty period, but we need a real remedy for non-conforming work.

ops.text: Garman further warrants that: (a) all services performed under this Agreement, including installation, data conversion, training and the Maintenance Services, will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards by suitably qualified personnel; (b) the Software will be free of viruses, worms, disabling code and other malicious code; and (c) Garman will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. If the Software fails to conform to the warranty in this Section 12, or any services fail to conform to the warranty in (a) above, Garman shall promptly repair or replace the Software, or re-perform the affected services, at no charge to Sparkling; if Garman fails to do so within thirty (30) days of written notice, Garman shall refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: No audit right binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the Agreement, so there is nothing to limit and no edit is warranted. The sections that would ordinarily host a usage-verification right contain none: § 2 (grant, p0028), § 3 use restrictions (p0031-p0039, which impose only substantive use limits with no verification or reporting mechanism), § 14 (confidentiality), § 17 (term and termination) and § 20 general matters (p0134-p0147). Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "access", "premises", "remote", "report", "books" and "right to enter" return no audit, inspection, records-examination, monitoring or system-access right running against us. The two near-hits are not audit rights: p0114 is an examination/testing right over escrow materials held by Sparkling (in our favour), and p0118 is a one-time post-termination certification that Sparkling has ceased use, not a recurring audit or any access to our systems. Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit

No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right over Sparkling. I confirmed this by reading the likely homes for such a right — § 2 (grant), § 3 plus its continuation (use restrictions, (a)–(g)), § 14 (confidentiality), § 20 and its continuation (general matters) — and by searching for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, compliance, records, access, premises, remote, certif*.

The only two near-hits both fall outside the rule:
- **p0114 (escrow)** — an examination/testing right held by *Sparkling*, i.e. in our favour.
- **p0118 (termination)** — a single post-termination certificate that Sparkling has ceased use; not a recurring audit and no access to our systems.

Because AUDIT constrains audit rights *binding the Customer*, their total absence sits at or above our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access). I deliberately recommend no edit here: proposing audit machinery would invite a right that does not currently exist. Worth monitoring only if Garman later seeks a verification clause in negotiation, at which point the preferred parameters should be inserted in § 3.
