paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 12 — Specifications and Warranty).**

What I found:
- **Duration is already compliant** — p0086 warrants Software conformance to Specifications for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter while under Maintenance Services. That meets/exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty.
- **No disclaimer risk** — the agreement contains no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer, so nothing swallows the express warranty.
- **Gaps:** Section 12 provides no remedy. The only repair path is Garman's "best efforts" repair under Software Repair Service (p0077), which is chargeable in five listed situations and offers no replacement or refund; the refund/rejection right (Sections 7–8) expires with the acceptance period. There is also no professional-and-workmanlike warranty for Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance), no no-malicious-code warranty, and no compliance-with-laws warranty.

Redline (validated ok:true): inserted a new paragraph after p0086 adding the services, malicious code and compliance warranties, plus an express repair/replace/re-perform remedy with a fee refund if Garman fails to cure within 30 days of notice. Comment flags the 90-day services-warranty fallback while holding firm on having a real remedy.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The Software conformance warranty duration meets the preferred position (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and continuing while under maintenance), and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer that would swallow it. However, Section 12 states no remedy for breach: the only repair path is Garman's "best efforts" repair under the Maintenance Services (p0077), which is fee-bearing in listed cases and carries no replacement or refund backstop, and the refund/rejection right in Sections 7-8 expires with the acceptance period. Section 12 also omits a professional and workmanlike warranty for Garman's services (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance), a no-malicious-code warranty and a compliance-with-laws warranty. We inserted those warranties and an express repair, replacement or re-performance remedy with a refund if Garman fails to cure within 30 days.

Original paragraphs:
p0086: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0086: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
Garman further warrants that: (a) all services performed under this Agreement, including installation, data conversion, training and the Maintenance Services, will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards by suitably qualified personnel; (b) the Software will be free of viruses, worms, disabling code and other malicious code; and (c) Garman will comply with all laws applicable to its performance under this Agreement. If the Software fails to conform to the warranty in this Section 12, or any services fail to conform to the warranty in (a) above, Garman shall promptly repair or replace the Software, or re-perform the affected services, at no charge to Sparkling; if Garman fails to do so within thirty (30) days of written notice, Garman shall refund the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 12 warrants Software conformance for a year but gives no stated remedy and says nothing about the services, malicious code or legal compliance, so we added a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus a repair, re-performance or refund remedy. If helpful we can accept a 90-day services warranty period, but we need a real remedy for non-conforming work.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (INSURANCE), confidence 0.90**

**What I found**

The Agreement has no insurance obligation at all — a full-text search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and Section 20 (General Matters, subsections (a)–(j)) covers time of the essence, notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractor, force majeure, severability, governing law, headings and entire agreement, with no coverage covenant.

**Why the rule bites**

Garman is not a hands-off licensor:
- **§ 4(a)** — Garman delivers copies and *installs the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location* (on-premises work).
- **§ 4(b)** — Garman performs *"conversion of Sparkling's data ... from its current electronic form"* for future installations (data processing).
- **§ 9(a)** — we must supply information about our operations and internal/external procedures.

That premises-plus-data profile is squarely the playbook trigger, and "no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises" is the walk-away position. The gap is compounded by **§ 15 (Limitation of Garman's Liability)** — with Garman's liability capped and no insurance behind it, uninsured exposure from on-site work or a data-conversion incident lands on us.

**Direction check:** the covenant runs against the counterparty (Garman), so this is not an obligation benefiting them that I should leave alone.

**The edit** (validated `ok:true` before submission)

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and the General Matters provisions (Section 20(a)-(j), p0135-p0149) contain no insurance covenant. Insurance is required here because Garman is not a mere shrink-wrap licensor: under Section 4(a) its personnel deliver and install the Software on our AS400s at each Authorized Location (on-premises work), and under Section 4(b) Garman performs conversion of "Sparkling's data" for future installations, with Section 9(a) requiring us to provide information about our operations and internal procedures. That combination of premises access and data processing is exactly the profile the playbook requires to be insured, and the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor that processes data or works on our premises. The gap is aggravated because Section 15 limits Garman's liability, so uninsured exposure would sit with us. The obligation runs against the counterparty, so there is no direction problem. Minimal fix: insert a new Section 20(k) after the entire-agreement subsection tracking the model language (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), surviving one year post-term. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is flagged in the comment if Garman cannot obtain the preferred limits.

Original paragraphs:
p0149: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
p0041: (a) In accordance with Schedule "C," Garman has delivered the required number of copies of the executable object code of the Software to those Authorized Locations (together with copies of the Documentation as is reasonably required by Sparkling to operate the Software in the manner contemplated hereunder) and installed the Software on the applicable AS400's at each Authorized Location. The installation of the Software at each existing Authorized Location shall be deemed to be completed including contracted changes and has been properly installed, is in good working order. Modifications and changes shall fall within the 60 day testing period at which time they are deemed to be completed and has been properly installed, is in good working order.
p0042: (b) For Future Installations and Conversions at an existing or new Authorized Location, Garman shall be available for Contracting required installation and conversion tasks as reasonably required, in consultation with and with the reasonable assistance of Sparkling, including conversion of Sparkling's data, as more particularly described in Schedule "D," from its current electronic form into a form suitable for processing with the Software and as required for the testing of the Software and for use of the Software as contemplated hereunder.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0149: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
(k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Garman processes, stores or has access to Sparkling's data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as Garman installs Software at our Authorized Locations and converts and accesses our data but carries no insurance obligation anywhere in the Agreement. Our position is CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M and cyber of USD 5M with certificates on request; we can discuss E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if the higher limits are unavailable.

**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The repair tightened the citations so they point only at the sections that *would* host an audit right rather than at near-hits that could be misread as audit language:

- **Cited as the locus of absence:** § 3 use restrictions (p0029, p0035, p0039) and § 20 general matters (p0134). § 3 imposes substantive use limits only — no verification, reporting or records mechanism attaches to them.
- **Coverage confirmed:** § 2 grant, § 14 confidentiality, § 17 term/termination and § 20 all read; searches for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, records, access, premises, remote, report, books, right to enter* all return nothing relevant.
- **Near-hits expressly excluded from the rule:** p0114 (escrow examination) runs in our favour; p0118 is a single post-termination destruction certificate, not a recurring audit and not system access.

On the failed deterministic check, I have kept the compliant status and recorded in the rationale why the signal is spurious: the "audit frequency limited" pattern cannot match where no audit clause exists. Inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters purely to satisfy the regex would manufacture an audit right against Sparkling that Garman does not currently have — the opposite of the rule's intent. If Garman later proposes any verification or usage-reporting clause, the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no access to our systems) should be inserted into § 3 at that point.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No audit right binding Sparkling exists anywhere in the Agreement, so there is nothing to limit and no edit is warranted. The sections that would ordinarily host a usage-verification right contain none: § 2 (grant, p0028), § 3 use restrictions (p0031-p0039, which impose only substantive use limits with no verification or reporting mechanism), § 14 (confidentiality), § 17 (term and termination) and § 20 general matters (p0134-p0147). Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "access", "premises", "remote", "report", "books" and "right to enter" return no audit, inspection, records-examination, monitoring or system-access right running against us. The two near-hits are not audit rights: p0114 is an examination/testing right over escrow materials held by Sparkling (in our favour), and p0118 is a one-time post-termination certification that Sparkling has ceased use, not a recurring audit or any access to our systems. Complete absence of an audit right is at least as favourable as the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and proposing audit machinery would risk inviting a right that does not presently exist. The failed deterministic check on "audit frequency limited" is a false signal: frequency-limiting language cannot be present where there is no audit clause to limit.

p0035: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
p0039: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.
p0134: 20. GENERAL MATTERS

**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment or volume restriction on us:

- **§ 11 (Fees, p0084)** — fees are payable simply "as set out in the Fee Schedule," with no committed spend, minimum quantity or shortfall mechanic.
- **§ 2 (p0028)** — additional fees arise only if we elect to use the Software at locations beyond the Authorized Locations, i.e. usage-based rather than committed.
- **§ 10 (p0065)** — maintenance is a "renewable one-year term," not a multi-year non-cancellable subscription.
- **§ 17(b) (p0118)** — we may terminate the entire Agreement at any time on 90 days' notice, so a clean exit exists.
- Targeted searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "volume", "quantity" and "non-cancellable" surfaced nothing binding us (the only "commitment" hit, p0143, is the standard no-agency clause).

This satisfies the preferred position (fees for usage or ordered services only), so no edit was needed.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-restriction obligation on Sparkling. Fees are payable only per the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken (§ 11, p0084), and additional locations trigger fees only if we choose to expand (§ 2, p0028). Maintenance runs on a renewable one-year term rather than a multi-year non-cancellable commitment (§ 10, p0065), and Sparkling may terminate the whole Agreement at any time on ninety days' notice (§ 17(b), p0118), so an exit exists. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay", "volume" and "quantity" returned no commitment language binding us. This meets the preferred position; no redline required.

p0118: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.

Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.

Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, monitoring or usage-verification right over Sparkling. I confirmed this by reading the likely homes for such a right — § 2 (grant), § 3 plus its continuation (use restrictions, (a)–(g)), § 14 (confidentiality), § 20 and its continuation (general matters) — and by searching for *audit, inspect, verify, examine, compliance, records, access, premises, remote, certif*.

The only two near-hits both fall outside the rule:
- **p0114 (escrow)** — an examination/testing right held by *Sparkling*, i.e. in our favour.
- **p0118 (termination)** — a single post-termination certificate that Sparkling has ceased use; not a recurring audit and no access to our systems.

Because AUDIT constrains audit rights *binding the Customer*, their total absence sits at or above our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access). I deliberately recommend no edit here: proposing audit machinery would invite a right that does not currently exist. Worth monitoring only if Garman later seeks a verification clause in negotiation, at which point the preferred parameters should be inserted in § 3.

**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

The repair tightened the citations so they point only at the sections that *would* host an audit right rather than at near-hits that could be misread as audit language:

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant, and no repair is available without worsening our position. The AUDIT rule caps a counterparty-favourable right; the Agreement grants Garman no such right at all. The sections that would host one contain none: § 2 grant (p0028), § 3 use restrictions (p0029-p0039, substantive use limits only, with no verification, reporting, records or access mechanism), § 14 confidentiality, § 17 term and termination, and § 20 general matters (p0134-p0147). Searches for audit, inspect, verify, examine, records, access, premises, remote, report, books and right to enter return no inspection, records-examination, monitoring or system-access right running against Sparkling. The two near-hits are not audit rights: p0114 is an examination and testing right over escrow materials held by Sparkling (in our favour), and p0118 is a one-time post-termination certification that Sparkling has ceased use, not a recurring audit and not access to our systems. Absence is strictly better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access), so the minimal edit is no edit. The recurring "audit frequency limited" check cannot pass on these facts: frequency-limiting words can only exist alongside an audit clause, and inserting them would manufacture an audit right against us that Garman does not currently hold - the opposite of the rule's intent. I am therefore holding the compliant status and flagging the check as not applicable for human override. If Garman later proposes any verification or usage-reporting clause, the preferred parameters should be inserted into § 3 at that time.

Original paragraphs:
p0029: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
p0035: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
p0039: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.
p0134: 20. GENERAL MATTERS

Findings:
[{"id":"f-ip-e046001f","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY","rationale":"Section 13 gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work \"including any Improvements or Modifications thereto\" — i.e. the bespoke Modifications (Schedule \"D\") that Sparkling commissions and pays for — with no licence back beyond the narrow, non-transferable use licence in Section 2. The Agreement contains no ownership provision for Sparkling's data at all, even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting Sparkling's data. That breaches the playbook position that we own what we pay for and retain all rights in our data. Garman's ownership of its pre-existing platform is acceptable, so the redline preserves that while vesting the paid-for Modifications in Sparkling (with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to any embedded Garman IP), confirming Sparkling's ownership of its data (including converted data), and excluding joint ownership.","proposal":"Limit Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Work, give Sparkling ownership of paid-for Modifications with a licence back to embedded Garman IP, and confirm Sparkling owns its data.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-765e9607","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 15 LIMITATION OF GARMAN'S LIABILITY","rationale":"Section 15 contains a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and already carves Sections 13 (IP ownership/indemnity, see p0090) and 14 (confidentiality) out of the limitation, but it contains no monetary aggregate cap at all. Direct-damages exposure is therefore unlimited for both parties, including for Sparkling as customer, which fails the playbook requirement of a meaningful mutual cap. The redline inserts a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable by Sparkling and USD 1,000,000, defines Excluded Claims (retaining Sections 13 and 14 and adding data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) as uncapped, and confirms Sparkling's fee obligations are not \"damages\" for cap purposes.","proposal":"Add a mutual monetary liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims and payment obligations excluded from the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-790f011c","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"PAGE 10","rationale":"Section 20(d) imposes a blanket assignment prohibition on both parties with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent — the playbook walk-away position. Section 3(c) compounds this by separately barring Sparkling from assigning absent Garman's written consent, and Section 2 grants only a \"non-transferable\" licence. There is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right elsewhere (Section 17 has no such trigger), so the fix is to add the affiliate/successor carve-out for us, a reasonableness standard for other assignments, a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors, and express confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) is conformed by cross-reference.","proposal":"Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling, reasonableness standard on consent, no competitor assignment by Garman, and no Garman right arising on our change of control","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-a892c356","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 GRANT OF LICENSE","rationale":"We reviewed the licence grant (§2), the restrictions on Sparkling's use (§3), maintenance and support (§10, including the Software Repair Service provisions) and fees (§11), and searched the whole agreement for \"exclusive\", \"sole\", \"requirements\", \"third part\" and \"compet\". The only uses of \"exclusive\" are (i) the non-exclusive licence grant to Sparkling in §2, (ii) the perpetual non-exclusive escrow-code licence to Sparkling (p0115), (iii) the exclusive-remedy provision in §15 and (iv) non-exclusive jurisdiction in the governing law clause — none of which is an exclusive-dealing or sole-supplier commitment. Section 3 imposes only software-use restrictions and contains no bar on procuring competing products or services from third parties, and nothing obliges Sparkling to source maintenance, improvements or future modules solely from Garman. Sparkling therefore retains full freedom to buy from other suppliers, which matches the preferred position; no redline is required (adding an affirmative non-exclusivity statement would be an unnecessary edit).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-7e042c0a","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY","rationale":"Section 13 (continuing at p0090) does contain a Garman-side IP indemnity tied to breach of its ownership/non-infringement warranty, with procure/modify/replace remedies (p0091-p0093) and no fee-only refund escape, and Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability cap (p0105) with survival confirmed in Section 18. So the walk-away and the \"indemnity absent / IP excluded\" triggers are not met, and there is no offsetting Sparkling indemnity to narrow. However, the clause falls short of our preferred position in four respects: (1) it is indemnify-and-hold-harmless only, with no obligation to defend third-party claims; (2) it covers only Sparkling and its officers and directors, not our affiliated companies, even though Section 2 licenses the Work for use by Sparkling affiliates at Authorized Locations; (3) there is no claim-handling procedure (control of defence, no settlement binding us without consent, cooperation), and the sole procedural term is a hard ten-calendar-day notice requirement with no materiality or prejudice qualifier, which risks being read as a condition precedent forfeiting the indemnity; and (4) the indemnity is limited to breach of the IP warranty and gives us nothing for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of our data or Confidential Information caused by Garman, or Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The redline inserts a single additional paragraph after p0093 supplying the defence duty, affiliate coverage, the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and the missing misconduct triggers, leaving the existing warranty indemnity and remedies intact as the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position.","proposal":"Add express defence obligation, affiliate coverage, claim-handling procedure and indemnity cover for Garman's breach of law, data breaches and wilful misconduct to Section 13.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-bb670a9e","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 FEES","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment penalty or minimum/early-termination fee payable by Sparkling. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"interest\" and \"shall pay\" return only Section 11 (payment of fees per the Fee Schedule). Section 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination charge, Section 17(c) converts the licence to a perpetual, fee-free licence and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees on Garman's default, and Section 8 requires Garman to refund all amounts if Sparkling rejects the Software. Section 19 non-solicitation carries no stipulated payment. All money flows on early exit therefore run in our favour, meeting the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-126cf1e0","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 GRANT OF LICENSE","rationale":"The grant is perpetual and not revocable at will (Section 17(a) keeps the licence in effect perpetually while fees are paid, with termination only on insolvency or uncured 30-day default), so the term aspect is compliant. However, the licence covers only affiliated companies \"operating at Authorized Locations\" and says nothing about contractors or outsourced service providers acting on our behalf, and it is expressly \"non-transferable\", reinforced by Section 3(c) and Section 20(d) which bar assignment without Garman's consent — leaving no successor-transfer path in an M&A transaction. We therefore added affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, a successor-transfer right, and conforming carve-outs in Sections 3(c) and 20(d).","proposal":"Extend the licence to Sparkling's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf and permit transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-792c00ed","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 RESTRICTIONS ON USE","rationale":"No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use), including the Page 2 continuation at 3(g), is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions (copying, assignment, reverse engineering, use of the Work, service-bureau use) and does not restrict the businesses Sparkling may operate or competing routing products it may buy or develop. Section 19 is a mutual one-year non-solicitation of employees, not a non-compete, and Section 14 confidentiality contains no residual bar on developing competing software (it expressly carves out independently developed information). Searches for \"compet\", \"exclusiv\", \"similar software\" and \"shall not develop\" returned no restrictive covenant against us, so the preferred position (no non-compete on Customer) is met and no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-21ea7cc0","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 19 NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES","rationale":"Section 19 binds us as well as the Vendor, but it is a no-hire (\"agree not to hire\"), not merely a non-solicit, and it extends to any employee of the other party regardless of involvement in the services, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. No-hire provisions and restrictions covering all Vendor personnel are walk-away items under the playbook. The clause is already mutual and one year in length, so rather than deleting it we narrowed it to the fallback: solicitation only, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.","proposal":"Convert mutual one-year no-hire into a narrow 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-a40612f0","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"PAGE 10","rationale":"The governing-law clause selects Nova Scotia/Canadian law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and non-exclusive venue leaves us exposed to suit in an unaccepted forum. No arbitration is required, so litigation-in-courts is already satisfied. We moved the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive state and federal courts in New York County) with a minimal edit to the jurisdiction and forum words only, and flagged Delaware/California or England and Wales (London courts) as fallbacks.","proposal":"Replace Nova Scotia governing law and venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-3775fee4","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 FEES","rationale":"The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity provision in either direction. Section 11 (Fees) simply requires Sparkling to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 10 / Page 5 (Maintenance and Support) impose service obligations on Garman with limited chargeable-repair exceptions at Garman's Fee Schedule rates; neither requires Sparkling to offer Garman terms no less favourable than those given to any third party or to match third-party offers. Targeted searches for \"most favoured/favored nation\", \"no less favourable\", \"parity\", \"best price\", \"lowest price\", \"match any\", \"competing offer\" and \"preferential\" returned no results, and the general provisions (Section 20) and other third-party references (Sections 3(f), 14 and the assignment clause) are unrelated to pricing. The preferred position of no MFN obligation burdening the Customer is therefore met; an MFN in our favour would be welcome but its absence is not a burden on us, so per the detection guidance no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-90fc6bcb","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 FEES","rationale":"The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-restriction obligation on Sparkling. Fees are payable only per the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken (§ 11, p0084), and additional locations trigger fees only if we choose to expand (§ 2, p0028). Maintenance runs on a renewable one-year term rather than a multi-year non-cancellable commitment (§ 10, p0065), and Sparkling may terminate the whole Agreement at any time on ninety days' notice (§ 17(b), p0118), so an exit exists. Searches for \"minimum\", \"commit\", \"shortfall\", \"take or pay\", \"volume\" and \"quantity\" returned no commitment language binding us. This meets the preferred position; no redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-a9391460","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 10 MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT","rationale":"Section 10 provides only a \"renewable one-year term\" for Maintenance Services and the Agreement contains no renewal mechanics: no renewal term length on renewal, no non-renewal notice window, no vendor renewal reminder, and no cap on maintenance fee uplift (Section 11 simply defers to the Fee Schedule, and no escalation language exists anywhere). Under a perpetual, fee-based term (17(a)) with prepaid maintenance fees, we should be able to exit on 30 days' notice and recover unused prepaid amounts.","proposal":"Shorten Sparkling's convenience termination notice to 30 days and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-44d76bb1","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 17 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 17 addresses only our obligations on termination (ceasing use and returning/destroying Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel, Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings 
**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product**

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified nineteen findings: two critical, seven high, seven medium and two low. Six positions are already compliant and need no edit (exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments and, on the facts, vendor audit rights).

The two critical items are: (i) **Section 13 vests all IP in Garman, including the bespoke Modifications we commission and pay for under Schedule "D"**, and the Agreement is silent on ownership of our data even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting it; and (ii) **Section 15 contains no monetary aggregate cap at all**, leaving direct-damages exposure unlimited on both sides. Section 15 does already carry a mutual consequential-damages exclusion and carve-outs for Sections 13 and 14, so the fix is additive rather than a rewrite.

The high-severity cluster concerns exit and portability: a blanket mutual assignment bar (Section 20(d), reinforced by Sections 2 and 3(c)) with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard; a licence grant limited to affiliates at Authorized Locations with no contractor or successor-transfer rights; a mutual one-year **no-hire** in Section 19 covering all personnel; and an IP indemnity in Section 13 that indemnifies but does not defend, omits our affiliates, has no claim-handling procedure and imposes a hard ten-day notice condition. Medium items are gap-fillers and forum: no maintenance renewal mechanics or fee-uplift cap, no transition assistance or data return on termination, a ninety-day convenience notice with no prepaid-fee refund, no remedy attached to the Section 12 warranty, and Nova Scotia governing law with non-exclusive venue. Vendor insurance is absent entirely despite on-premises installation and data conversion.

One finding — the AUDIT analysis — failed automated verification and is carried as **needs_review** pending human sign-off; substantively the Agreement grants Garman no audit right against us, which is better than our preferred position, so we propose no edit.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications thereto", i.e. the paid-for Modifications; no data-ownership provision at all. Limit Garman's ownership to its pre-existing Work, vest paid-for Modifications in us with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back to embedded Garman IP, confirm we own our data (including converted data), exclude joint ownership. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary aggregate cap; direct-damages exposure unlimited for both parties. Insert a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (retaining §§ 13 and 14; adding data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and fee obligations excluded from the cap. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 (§ 20(d); see also §§ 2, 3(c), 17) | Blanket mutual assignment bar, no affiliate/M&A carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard, no change-of-control right. Add affiliate/successor carve-out, reasonableness on consent, bar on assignment to our competitors, and confirmation that our change of control gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right; conform § 3(c). |
| 4 | High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Indemnity exists and is carved out of the § 15 cap, but is hold-harmless only (no defence duty), omits our affiliated companies, has no claim-handling procedure, imposes a hard 10-day notice with no prejudice qualifier, and covers only IP warranty breach. Add one paragraph supplying defence, affiliate coverage, notice/control/cooperation mechanics and triggers for breach of law, unauthorized access/disclosure of our data or Confidential Information, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual term is compliant, but the grant reaches only affiliates "operating at Authorized Locations", omits contractors acting on our behalf, and is expressly non-transferable with no successor path. Extend to affiliates and contractors, add successor-transfer right, conform §§ 3(c) and 20(d). |
| 6 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Mutual, but drafted as a **no-hire** covering any employee of the other party with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Narrow to a 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services (running from end of involvement) with advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | Only non-exclusive licence/escrow grants, exclusive-remedy and non-exclusive jurisdiction references; no exclusive-dealing or sole-supplier commitment. No edit. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late-payment or early-termination charge; §§ 8, 17(b) and 17(c) run refunds and exit rights in our favour. No edit. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | § 3 is limited to conventional licence-scope restrictions; § 19 is a non-solicitation, and § 14 carves out independently developed information. No edit. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 | Nova Scotia/Canadian law with non-exclusive Nova Scotia jurisdiction; no arbitration required. Move to New York law and exclusive state and federal courts in New York County; Delaware/California or England and Wales (London) as fallbacks. |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Only a "renewable one-year term"; no renewal length, opt-out window, reminder or uplift cap. Add successive 12-month renewals, 30-day customer opt-out, 60-day Garman reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%/60 days). |
| 12 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination | Our convenience right sits at fallback only: 90 days' notice and no refund of prepaid fees (the 17(c) refund applies only on Garman default; § 8 only on rejection). Shorten to 30 days and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17 covers only our return/destruction obligations; no transition assistance, no return of our data, no deletion or certification. Insert new § 17(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification) and add to the § 18 survival list. |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Duration is compliant and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer, but no remedy is stated (only "best efforts" fee-bearing repair under maintenance), and services, no-malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranties are absent. Add those warranties plus repair/replace/re-perform with refund if Garman fails to cure within 30 days. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or pricing-parity provision in either direction. No edit. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees | Fees payable only for licence and services taken; additional-location fees are elective; maintenance is a renewable one-year term; § 17(b) exit available. No edit. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 11 (§ 20 General Matters) | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite on-premises installation under § 4(a) and conversion of our data under § 4(b), and with Garman's liability limited by § 15. Insert new § 20(k): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, surviving one year post-term (fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |
| 18 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 3 Restrictions on Use | Garman holds no audit, inspection, records or system-access right against us — better than our preferred position — so the minimal edit is no edit. The automated "audit frequency limited" check cannot pass without manufacturing an audit right; flagged for human override. If Garman later proposes any verification or usage-reporting clause, insert the preferred parameters into § 3 then. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as playbook walk-away positions and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Assignment (Page 10, § 20(d)).** A blanket assignment prohibition with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent is the playbook walk-away position, compounded by § 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in § 2.
2. **Non-solicitation (§ 19).** No-hire provisions, and restrictions extending to all Vendor personnel regardless of involvement, are walk-away items. We have proposed narrowing rather than deletion.
3. **Vendor insurance (Page 11).** No insurance for a vendor that processes our data and works on our premises is the walk-away position; the gap is aggravated by the § 15 limitation of Garman's liability.

For completeness, the findings confirm the **indemnity** walk-away triggers (indemnity absent / IP excluded) are **not** met, because § 13 contains a Garman-side IP indemnity with procure/modify/replace remedies, no fee-only refund escape, a § 15 carve-out and § 18 survival.

## Next steps

1. **Priority redlines to Garman:** IP ownership of paid-for Modifications and our data (§ 13) and the mutual liability cap with Excluded Claims (§ 15). These two drive the commercial risk profile and should lead the markup.
2. **Second tier:** assignment/change of control (§ 20(d), conforming § 3(c)), licence scope for affiliates, contractors and successors (§ 2), the § 13 indemnity paragraph (defence, affiliates, procedure, misconduct triggers), and the § 19 non-solicit narrowing.
3. **Gap-fillers to table together:** maintenance renewal mechanics and uplift cap (§ 10), transition assistance, data return and certified deletion as new § 17(d) with § 18 survival, 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund (§ 17(b)), warranty remedies and additional warranties (§ 12), and the insurance covenant as new § 20(k).
4. **Forum:** propose New York law and exclusive New York County courts; hold Delaware/California or England and Wales (London) in reserve as fallbacks.
5. **Internal confirmations needed:** (a) business sign-off on the fallback insurance limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) if Garman cannot meet the preferred limits; (b) sign-off on the renewal uplift fallback (5% / 60 days); and (c) reviewer override on the AUDIT finding, which failed automated verification — we recommend confirming "no edit" so we do not manufacture an audit right against us.
6. **No action** on exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN and minimum commitments; these are compliant and we will not open them.
"}
